land.text: the Khalkha tumen of Dayan Khan's Left Wing, 'the largest of the six tümens' under Gersenji (Northern Yuan page), on the lands of present-day central Mongolia; from 1547 (the year Cliopatria's Mongol Khanate loses them, mongol-khanate ledger) the Khalkha are drawn as a state, though the Great Khan stayed their nominal overlord until 'the Khalkha and Oirat Mongols no longer obeyed his authority' under Ligdan Khan (r. 1604-1634); after Ligdan's death in 1634 'the Mongols formed four Khanates', the Khalkha ones holding Outer Mongolia

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Mongol Khanate row ends in 1635/2 (Ejei Khan's surrender); the golden-horde dossier (ia-02-x) re-attributes its 'Golden Horde' rows 1636-1691 (Mongolia) to the Khalkha khanates.

land.text: 'Galdan led 30,000 Dzungar troops into Outer Mongolia in 1688 and defeated Chikhundorj in three days'

successors.note: The Khalkha leaders appealed to the Qing and returned as Qing vassals after Galdan fell; Outer Mongolia is Qing territory from 1691 (OM) or 1696 (the dzungar-khanate dossier).

capitals.note: NY: 'The Tushetu Khans at Ulaanbaatar'; the pages give no capital and no coordinates; those are the gazetteer's Ulaanbaatar, a stand-in for the nomadic seat. [fx-45: from 1547 with the state's new start; the Tüsheet Khan's seat is only a stand-in for the nomadic centre of the Khalkha lands, which the Khalkha page puts in the Khangai ('Dwelling in the Khangai Mountains') and 'central Mongolia'.]

Altan Khan of the Tumed page: in 1547 'Altan forced Bodi Alagh's successor Darayisung Küdeng Khan to flee eastward'; 'In 1552 Altan Khan gained control of the remains of Karakorum'; 'Altan Khan died on 13 January 1582'. The Tumed dossier gives these lands up in 1582 to the name 'khalkha' (nobody), so they stay grey until the 1636 keyframe unless its ledger 3 is pointed at khalkha-khanates.

The Khalkha floor is Mongolia without Western Mongolia (about 1.26 M km2): the rows are 1.8-2.3 times larger because they run into Inner Mongolia (already Manchu by 1636, NY) and Transbaikalia (Russian from the 1640s, KHA). The pages give no area. Same floor shape for the whole span, confidence 1 before 1636: the Northern Yuan page says Dayan Khan's youngest son Gersenji 'became the ruler of the Khalkha Mongols, the largest of the six tümens' (undated), the Khalkha page that Dayan Khan 'created the Khalkha Tumen out of Mongols residing in the territory of present-day central Mongolia' (undated) and that from 1628 the Selenge valley was 'under the rule of the Khalkha khans'; neither page dates a Khalkha extent in the 16th century.] [Review fx-45, 3 Nov 2026: from back to 1636; the years 1547-1635 are the new keyframe khalkha-khanates_1547, which leaves out the Tumed lands of Altan Khan.]

ledger.note: 1547: the Khalkha lands are drawn as a state in their own right, the year Cliopatria's mislabelled 'Golden Horde' row takes Mongolia over from the Mongol Khanate (mongol-khanate ledger 9, a loss of 'northern and central Mongolia' in 1547, confidence 1). The pages date no Khalkha independence: 'Dayan Khan ... youngest son Gersenji Khongtaiji of the Jalayir became the ruler of the Khalkha Mongols, the largest of the six tümens' (Northern Yuan page, undated); 'By the reign of Ligdan Khan (r. 1604-1634), the Eastern Mongol tumens had ceased to function as a unified entity' and 'the Khalkha and Oirat Mongols no longer obeyed his authority'; 'After Ligdan Khan's death in 1634, the Mongols formed four Khanates'; Ejei Khan surrendered to the Qing in February 1635; the Tüsheet Khan Gombodorj 'retained his independence and suzerainty over the Sechen and Jasagtu khans'. The earlier dating of this event to 1636 (the end of Cliopatria's Mongol Khanate row) is now the date of the three khanates, not of the state. [Review fx-45, 3 Nov 2026: the region leaves out the tumed dossier's Mongolian lands (its 1547 found, its 1552 gains of Karakorum and the south Gobi), which the floor shape had taken from it by the size rule; 'In 1552 Altan Khan gained control of the remains of Karakorum' (Altan Khan of the Tumed page). They come to the Khalkha with the 1636 keyframe.]

region.text: the Khalkha lands: Outer Mongolia without the Oirat west; the pages name no component, only 'Outer Mongolia' and 'the Khalkha khans ruling Outer Mongolia'

ledger.note: 1688: Galdan conquers Khalkha Mongolia. 'Galdan led 30,000 Dzungar troops into Outer Mongolia in 1688 and defeated Chikhundorj in three days'; the Khalkha 'had to seek help from the Kangxi Emperor' (KHA). After Galdan's fall (he died in 1697) 'the Khalkha leaders returned to Outer Mongolia as Qing vassals' (NY). OM's infobox dates the Qing seizure of northern Khalkha to 1691; the dzungar-khanate dossier has the Qing take Outer Mongolia in 1696.

wars.name: Khalkha war with the Qing (Gombodorj)
wars.outcome: No decisive result: 'In 1647, Gombodorj met the Qing in battle with 50,000 cavalry'; from 1655 the Qing interfered by appointing their own lamas.
wars.note: No territory changed hands on the pages.

wars.name: Khalkha-Russian frontier disputes in Transbaikalia
wars.outcome: Russian incursions into Transbaikalia (the Khori of the Uda surrendered to the Russians in 1647; the Khalkha khans protested by 1652; Khalkha raiding parties reached Bratsk, Ilimsk, Yeravninsk and Nerchinsk from 1666).
wars.note: The land on the Uda and in Transbaikalia is outside the Khalkha floor and no frontier is dated.

wars.name: Dzungar conquest of Khalkha
wars.outcome: Chikhundorj killed Shira in 1687; Galdan invaded in 1688 and beat Chikhundorj in three days while Siberian Cossacks beat a 10,000-man Khalkha army near Lake Baikal; the Khalkha appealed to Kangxi.

certainty.note: Fix fx-45: the Khalkha tumen's pastures in central Mongolia under their own princes, nominally under the Northern Yuan Great Khan; neither the Northern Yuan nor the Khalkha page dates a Khalkha extent before 1636, so the floor shape of 1636-1688 is carried back (confidence 1).
Nomadic khanates with no surveyed frontier; the Russian frontier in Transbaikalia was disputed.

notes:
Written for batch ia-03-x from three pages (NY, KHA, OM; budget 3-5). A state Cliopatria lacks: its land is drawn by 15 mislabelled 'Golden Horde' rows (1636-1695) that the golden-horde dossier (ia-02-x) marks wrong; this dossier supplies the corrected shape. None of the pages gives the Khalkha land, an area, a capital, the founding dates of the khanates (Abtai Khan and the 1586 Erdene Zuu, the 1640 Mongol-Oirat Code and the 1691 Dolon Nor assembly are all absent from the three pages) or the Treaty of Nerchinsk; the shape is the researcher's floor.
End date: OM dates 'Seizure of northern Khalkha: 1691' (Qing), the dzungar-khanate dossier (ia-03-d) dates the Dzungar conquest to August 1688 and the Qing taking of Outer Mongolia to June 1696. 1688 is followed because NY dates Galdan's conquest to 1688; the Qing take over in 1696 and an Outer Mongolia colony dossier is a gap (the Qing dossier should carry it). The 1688-1696 years are Dzungar-held on that dossier. Counterparts: mongol-khanate (ia-02), dzungar-khanate (ia-03-d), qing-dynasty (ea-08), tsardom-of-russia (eu).

Fix fx-45 (2 Nov 2026), 1547-1635. The state now starts in 1547 instead of 1636: the mongol-khanate dossier ends in 1635 but loses northern and central Mongolia at 1547 (its ledger 9, 'khalkha'), and no other dossier drew Mongolia in 1547-1635, so the map showed it grey for 89 years. The extent is the floor shape of 1636-1688 at confidence 1; the Northern Yuan and Khalkha pages give the Khalkha as a tumen of Dayan Khan's Left Wing with their own rulers, undated, and Ligdan's reign (1604-1634) as the time they 'no longer obeyed' the Great Khan. The founding of the three khanates (1634-1636) is a later step inside the same state. ROUTE TO OWNER: mongol-khanate ledger 9 names the counterpart 'khalkha', which is not a slug; it should read khalkha-khanates.

Review fx-45 (3 Nov 2026). The 1547-1635 extent is now its own keyframe, khalkha-khanates_1547, and the 1547 found has the same region: the floor shape without the tumed dossier's Mongolian lands (Cliopatria's Tümed shapes of 1547 and 1552 and the Karakorum disc; Altan Khan of the Tumed page: 'In 1552 Altan Khan gained control of the remains of Karakorum'), which the size rule had given to this smaller state. khalkha-khanates_1636 again starts in 1636 and takes them back from nobody.
